The run evaluates, on new seeds, a protocol amended after partial calibration exposure; it is not a fully blind confirmation. 
The primary result is the whole curve over the nine values of $r$. No value of $r$ is selected or used to summarize it.

The tiers ran in the fixed order, without changes based on AUC, band width or invalidity. The declared-close rule requires all unfinished work to stop. 
Only complete units contribute boundaries and AUC profiles; every other unit appears in the inventory with its status. 
All nine tier-\resultnum{v4.protocol.tier.main_B}{1} units of B were complete and valid. The main curve is therefore valid under the frozen rule. 
Against B, the first boundary was classified as small ($\resultnum{v4.protocol.a.0}{0}<a^*\le \resultnum{v4.protocol.small_cut}{0.03}$) at \resultnum{v4.t1.n_small}{[n]} values of $r$ and large ($\resultnum{v4.protocol.small_cut}{0.03}<a^*\le \resultnum{v4.protocol.a.090}{0.90}$) at \resultnum{v4.t1.n_large}{[n]}. The cut at \resultnum{v4.protocol.small_cut}{0.03} is an internal convention, not a demonstrated effect size, and boundaries are grid strengths, not continuous estimates. 
The attained first boundaries ranged from $a=\resultnum{v4.t1.first_min}{[a]}$ to $a=\resultnum{v4.t1.first_max}{[a]}$, and at every value of $r$ where $a^*$ was attained the sustained boundary equalled it. 
At \resultnum{v4.t1.n_crossing}{[n]} values of $r$, the lower band exceeded \resultnum{v4.protocol.target}{0.70} at some strength; ``crossing'' refers only to such strengths. 
The inverted interval of $a^*$ spanned at most one grid step at all \resultnum{v4.t1.n_attained}{[n]} values of $r$ where $a^*$ was attained. This meets the frozen precision target, which is a planning goal rather than a statement of power.

Mechanisms are therefore not compared, either locally or in the headline. Tables and figures are retained for all valid units. 
Fig.~\ref{fig:v4-F1} and Table~\ref{tab:v4-T1} show trait-plus-autoregressive persistence (B) and state-dependent persistence (D) side by side at all \resultnum{v4.bd.n_side_by_side}{[n]} response signal shares ($r=$ \resultnum{v4.bd.r_side_by_side}{[r list]}). Per-cell nuisance diagnostics, namely the mean shift, the Monte Carlo error of the nuisance variance and the fraction of projected draws, are released with every cell.
